newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Haider aims to force referendum on euro.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Haider aims to force referendum on euro.

text.p: Austrian Freedom Party (FPOe) head Joerg Haider said in a television interview late on Sunday his far-right party planned to force a referendum on the introduction of Europe's single currency.
"Who's stopping us from saying 'Let's postpone this development because the time is not yet ripe for it' and who hinders us from asking the people?" he said.
He said he would propose a petition for the referendum to the FPOe executive on Monday.

Haider argued that a single European currency, the euro, was currently not economically justifiable and said he doubted the coalition government's pledge that the euro would be as strong as Austria's schilling.
Austria should also renegotiate its contributions to the European Union (EU) because although it was a small country, Austria was paying the third highest net contributions to the EU, he said.
Haider also reiterated that he was optimistic of becoming chancellor in 1999.
The FPOe is the country's third strongest party and Europe's biggest far-right parliamentary grouping.
